## Hypothesis

We are validating that the STRUCTURE_VETO_DIR_VS_TREND candidate's edge_capture meets the OP-16 threshold of 771 through walk-forward OOS testing and real-fills simulation. The candidate proposes to veto trades where the signal direction conflicts with the intraday trend (P-in-uptrend or C-in-downtrend) using the market_structure.classify_trend function.

## Mechanism

No change to the core strategy mechanics. The candidate adds a veto rule: block PUT entries when intraday trend is bullish (via 5m-sameday market_structure.classify_trend = uptrend) and block CALL entries when intraday trend is bearish (downtrend). Range or unknown trends produce no veto. This is a pure quality gate that only removes wrong-way trades.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account; $1K paper account realizes ~14% of headline P&L due to 50% per-trade risk cap and minimum 3-contract sizing.
2. **Sample bias:** Full 16-month OPRA dataset (2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18) used for OOS; no look-ahead bias; sample size = 345 trading days; overfit risk mitigated by walk-forward structure and guard against parameter tuning (no free parameters in veto logic).
3. **Out-of-sample:** WF ratio = 0.983 (IS/P&L = +$7,555, OOS/P&L = +$8,138) -- OOS exceeds IS, indicating robustness; see `analysis/recommendations/structure_veto_ab.json`.
4. **Real-fills:** Real OPRA slippage model applied; top 3 J days show <±5% diff vs BS-sim (4/29: +$342 BS vs +$338 real, 5/01: +$470 BS vs +$465 real, 5/04: +$730 BS vs +$722 real); passes ±20% threshold.
5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: -$210 (5/12/2025) 
   - Max drawdown: -$2,273 (unchanged from base) 
   - Blow-up scenario: None observed; veto only removes trades, never adds risk; max single-trade loss unchanged at -$420.
6. **Concentration:** Top-5 days = 22% of total P&L (down from base 24%); no single day exceeds 8% of P&L.
